backend.title: What is a backend?
backend.intro: The backend is the part of an app that runs on a server and handles requests. Say you add The Hobbit to your book club’s list on your phone. A minute later, Mira sees it on her laptop. How did it get there?

steps.title: You tap Save
steps.body: The frontend is the part you see and use. It shows the book title and the Save button. When you tap it, the app sends the title and the club’s list ID to the backend.

steps.title: The backend checks the rules
steps.body: Can you edit this list? Did you send a title? The backend checks both before saving. Six spaces and an enthusiastic tap still don’t count as a book.

steps.title: Mira opens the list
steps.body: Once the checks pass, the backend saves the entry in a database and tells your phone it worked. When Mira opens the list, her laptop asks the backend for the latest books. There’s The Hobbit.

steps.title: In short
steps.body: The frontend takes your tap, the backend decides what to do, and the database remembers the book.

lifecycle.title: The request lifecycle
lifecycle.intro: Mira taps The Hobbit to see its details. One tap starts a round trip from her browser to the server and back. That trip is the request lifecycle.

steps.title: Ask for the book
steps.body: The browser sends the request below. GET means “read,” and 42 is the book’s ID. Together they ask, “Can I have the details for book 42?”
steps.code: GET /books/42

steps.title: Find the answer
steps.body: The server directs the request to a handler, the function that knows how to look up a book. It checks that Mira can read the list, then asks the database for entry 42.

steps.title: Send it back
steps.body: The server replies with a status and the book data. Here, 200 means the lookup worked. Mira’s browser reads the title and displays it. If the book is missing, the server can send 404 instead.
steps.code:
200 OK
{"title": "The Hobbit"}

steps.title: In short
steps.body: A request carries the question to the server. A response carries the answer back.

runtime.title: Run your first Node.js program
runtime.intro: Node.js runs JavaScript outside a browser. Start with a file that prints one line, before opening a network connection.

steps.title: Check the runtime
steps.body: Install Node.js from nodejs.org, open a terminal, and check that your shell can find it. A version number means you can run a script.
steps.code: node --version

steps.title: Run a file
steps.body: Save the first line below in hello.mjs. Run the command from the same folder. Edit the message and run it again to see where the output comes from.

steps.title: Inspect the process
steps.body: Type node in your terminal to open its interactive prompt. Evaluate the expression below to see the folder your program starts in. Type .exit to leave.
steps.code: process.cwd()

modules.title: Organize code and packages
modules.intro: Split book formatting from the script that uses it.

steps.title: Export a function
steps.body: Save this in book.mjs. A named export makes the function available to other modules.

steps.title: Import it
steps.body: Save this in main.mjs beside book.mjs and run node main.mjs. The relative path identifies your local module.
steps.code:
import { label } from './book.mjs';
console.log(label({ title: 'Dune' }));

steps.title: Manage dependencies
steps.body: Run npm init -y in a new project folder to create package.json. npm install followed by a package name records that dependency. Commit the lockfile so teammates can reproduce the resolved versions.
steps.code:
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev typescript

async.title: Files, promises, and the event loop
async.intro: Predict the three messages before you run this example in an .mjs file.

steps.title: Start a read
steps.body: A file read takes time. The promise represents its eventual result. Node can continue running the rest of this script while the read is pending.

steps.title: Yield and resume
steps.body: Append these lines. The first two messages are start and pending. After the read completes, the suspended function resumes and reports the character count.

steps.title: Handle failure
steps.body: Try reading a missing file inside a try block. A rejected promise at an await jumps to catch. Long synchronous calculations still occupy the JavaScript thread and delay other handlers.
steps.code:
try { await readFile('missing.txt'); }
catch (error) { console.error(error.message); }

http.title: Serve an HTTP response
http.intro: Turn a script that exits into a process that listens for requests.

steps.title: Start listening
steps.body: Save this as server.mjs and run node server.mjs. listen keeps the process waiting for connections on your computer.

steps.title: Inspect the exchange
steps.body: Open this address in a browser. Refresh it and the handler runs again. In the browser Network panel inspect the status, content type, and body. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

streams.title: Streams and events
streams.intro: A large file can travel through a program one chunk at a time.

steps.title: Connect a pipeline
steps.body: Put books.txt beside this .mjs script, then run the script in that folder. The pipeline reads chunks and writes a copy. Await its promise to detect completion or catch failures.

steps.title: Match the reader to the writer
steps.body: A slow destination needs time to drain its buffer. The pipeline regulates the reader so it can process a file larger than the available memory.
steps.code: source → buffered chunks → destination

steps.title: Listen for an event
steps.body: An event emitter lets a producer notify listeners. Register the listener first. Each emit below calls it with the supplied title.

operate.title: Configure, debug, and test
operate.intro: Make the reading-list service easier to run and check.

steps.title: Read configuration
steps.body: Environment variables arrive as strings. This expression chooses a port when PORT is missing and converts it to a number. Validate the range before passing user-supplied configuration to listen.
steps.code: const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);

steps.title: Inspect a running script
steps.body: Launch the server with the inspector and a breakpoint at startup. Attach a Node debugger, step into the handler, and inspect req.url when a request arrives.
steps.code: node --inspect-brk server.mjs

steps.title: Test a rule
steps.body: Put this in book.test.mjs beside book.mjs from the modules lesson. Run node --test. Change the expected value and read the difference in the failure report.

js-books.title: Write a book handler in JavaScript
js-books.intro: Give your API one rule: a book must have a nonempty title.

steps.title: Define the boundary
steps.body: Incoming JSON can contain any value. Check its shape before calling string methods.

steps.title: Try two inputs
steps.body: Save the function and these calls in book.mjs. Run node book.mjs. The first call prints Dune and the second reports the validation error.
steps.code:
console.log(titleOf(' Dune '));
try { titleOf(42); } catch { console.log('Invalid title'); }

documents.title: Store books in MongoDB
documents.intro: Use mongosh connected to a local MongoDB instance.

steps.title: Model a book
steps.body: Switch to a practice database. Each book will be a document in the books collection. MongoDB creates the collection on its first insert.
steps.code: use reading_list

steps.title: Save and read
steps.body: Insert a document and find it by title. Keep the generated identifier to update this exact book.
steps.code:
const book = db.books.insertOne({title: 'Dune', finished: false});
db.books.findOne({_id: book.insertedId})

steps.title: Update and delete
steps.body: Mark this book as finished. Read it back before removing the practice document.
steps.code:
db.books.updateOne({_id: book.insertedId}, {$set: {finished: true}})
db.books.findOne({_id: book.insertedId})
db.books.deleteOne({_id: book.insertedId})

typed-books.title: Write a book handler in TypeScript
typed-books.intro: Give your API one rule: a book must have a nonempty title.

steps.title: Define the boundary
steps.body: Incoming JSON can contain any value. Check its shape before calling string methods.

steps.title: Try two inputs
steps.body: Save the function and these calls in book.ts. Install TypeScript with npm install -D typescript, then run npx tsc --strict book.ts and node book.js. Observe which checks still happen at runtime.
steps.code:
console.log(titleOf(' Dune '));
try { titleOf(42); } catch { console.log('Invalid title'); }

tables.title: Store books in PostgreSQL
tables.intro: Use psql connected to a practice PostgreSQL database.

steps.title: Model a book
steps.body: Create a table. Each row needs an identifier and a title. A primary key lets the database distinguish two books with the same title.
steps.code: CREATE TABLE books (id integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, title text NOT NULL, finished boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false);

steps.title: Save and read
steps.body: Insert a row and read the generated id. Use it in the next step to select the intended row.
steps.code:
INSERT INTO books (title) VALUES ('Dune') RETURNING id;
SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE title = 'Dune';

steps.title: Update and delete
steps.body: Replace 1 with the returned id. Mark the book finished, inspect the row, then remove the practice record.
steps.code:
UPDATE books SET finished = true WHERE id = 1 RETURNING *;
DELETE FROM books WHERE id = 1;
